title: Introduce cost-surgeon prefill sieves and quant pruning
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: reduce per-token cost for mixed workloads by adding a lightweight prefill filtering layer (prefill sieves) plus a conservative quant-pruning step that trims redundant weight blocks for inference on quantized variants. This PR implements a first-pass, tenant-scoped prefill sieve that quickly classifies requests by prefill utility score and applies three default policies: allow, coalesce, or defer to background warmup. We couple that with a pluggable quant pruning pipeline that runs as part of the model preparation step and produces compact quant profiles optimized for short-sequence chat workloads. The changes aim to improve unit economics for bursty traffic without sacrificing latency SLOs. Scope: runtime prefill logic, model builder hooks for quant pruning, CLI tooling to preview cost impact, e2e tests, docs, and a migration helper. Backwards compatibility: default policies are opt-in via tenant defaults and the runtime falls back to previous behavior when the feature flag is off. Rollout plan: gated canary to 10% tenants for 48h, collect unit-econ telemetry, then gradual ramp to 100% with auto-rollback on cost or latency regression. Checklist: 1) implement prefill sieve runtime and policy mapping. 2) add quant pruning model hook and profile serializer. 3) add cost-preview CLI for operators. 4) add integration and load tests that simulate mixed bursty chat and embedding traffic. 5) update docs and release notes. 6) add telemetry metrics and dashboards. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2318/prefill-sieves-quant-pruning and the playbook in docs/ops/cost-surgeon.md. Summary of changes and rationale below.

review_comments: Andre Gomez: Great direction. Please add unit tests for the scorer edge cases where prefill utility ties across sequences. Also ensure the default scoring weights are documented in the operator guide.
Maya Chen (author): Added tie-break unit tests and documented default weights in docs. See commit c9d8b71.
Priya Nair: Telemetry looks good but we need a histogram for 'prefill_delay_ms' to detect regressions when we defer requests. Can you add that?
Maya Chen: Added histogram prefills.delay_ms and updated dashboards. See commit f4a6c2b.

Liam O'Connor: Quant pruning implementation seems conservative. Please ensure pruning is disabled for models with rare ops or for tenants who opted out. Also, add a safety throttle to pruning so we do not change more than 5% of blocks per build by default.
Maya Chen: Respect tenant opt-out and safety throttle added, configurable via deploy/feature_flags/cost_surgeon.yaml.
